title: Female Son
paragraphs: Perched beside the greenish bushes of the garden, Marakatam and Taṅkam were discussing sweet nothings. “You, Taṅkam, do you know the scoop! It is widely believed that our Aṉṉam is mentally disturbed, of late.”
“Why? Is there any heartbreak due to love failure? As far as I know, she has not fallen for anybody and none is in love with her, either.”
“I also suspected on the same lines and paid her a visit yesterday.”
“You saw her in person? How is she? Is she blabbering anything?”
“Yes. I saw her in person! She was in the midst of a junk of books!”
“Junk of books? Or useless books?”

“Aṉṉam is never known to have even touched them! She completely abhors such books and for that matter, even odd perverted stories published in weeklies. She discards them, even if they are offered by somebody.”

“Let it be so. Though men and women feign to dislike them, they never miss any opportunity to read them, unnoticed by others. Okay, Marakatam! Aṉṉam always remains engrossed in literature. What has happened to her now?”
“That is why she is afflicted with literature craze.”
“You are also a connoisseur of literature,”
“Not to such an extent as to confuse myself and others too.”
“Please tell me, what is the matter?”
“A bisexual deprived of manliness should not be referred to using musculine verbal suffixes; we should, according to norms of grammar, use feminine suffixes.”
“That is correct! So what? What does Aṉṉam say?”
“She says the term female son (peṇ makaṉ) could be used.”
“How could it be? Female son? Are you referring to a eunuch?”
“No, no! Seems, it was in vogue to call the girls in pre-pubescent stage by the term female son. That is why Aṉṉam says ‘female son came’ (with feminine verbal suffix) could very well be used.”
“Okay, okay. There is no denying the fact that she has gone bonkers! She is fantasizing quite interestingly. Lunatic, lunatic! She is no doubt a lunatic!”
“Who is mad? You Taṅkam! Marakatam! It is not my own concept!”
A shouting Aṉṉam made her appearance with Tolkāppiyam in her hand. She opened the relevant page and said sarcastically, “Here, open your eyes properly and read this:
> The nominal terms ellārum and ellīrum > And the term makaṉ that follows peṇ > Are of the same kind too, > [They mark distinctions of gender within the human-class], > So do the learned say.
Again,
> The aberrant feminine gender designation peṇmakaṉ > Takes the verb concord > In the manner of a feminine gender denoting term.
Do you know what this verse in Collatikāram means? To put it in a nutshell:
The expression female son, which is a breach of gender, would take feminine gender—‘the girl came’(with the feminine verbal suffix).”
Aṉṉam elucidated further: “Terms like ‘everybody’. ‘all persons’ and female son are human class words. In the past, it was in vogue to call girls in pre-pubescent phase by the term female son.”
Taṅkam and Marakatam were completely astonished and listened to Aṉṉam without blinking their eyelids.
“Here is the Tolkāppiyam verse. Read it as well as its commentary first and decide as to whether Aṉṉam is really mad.” Thus thundered Aṉṉam and made her exit.
> The nominal terms ellārum and ellīrum > And the term makaṉ that follows peṇ > Are of the same kind too,
> [They mark distinctions of gender within the human-class], > So do the learned say. > > (Collatikāram : Peyariyal, verse 10)
> The aberrant feminine gender designation peṇmakaṉ > Takes the verb concord > In the manner of a feminine gender denoting term. > > (Collatikāram : Peyariyal, verse 40)
